overview.lead: Leatherworkers make gear for leather and mail wearers plus armor kits, and Forever adds kits that give stats as well as armor.

points.text: Blizzard says the more advanced recipes need a Tanning Rack, so the skill-140 camp object matters early.

heldBack.text: Icy Veins points Druids, Hunters, Rogues and Shamans toward Leatherworking.
heldBack.reason: No graded fact holds the class recommendation.

101.summary: What Leatherworking makes in Forever, its camp objects and how to level it.

steps.text: Open the professions window with K, then search or filter the recipe list and track a recipe in the objectives frame.
Place a Camp Tent at skill 20, a Tanning Rack at 140 and a Sewing Machine at 300. The Tanning Rack blueprint drops from Razorclaw the Butcher in Shadowfang Keep.
Get the Tanning Rack blueprint before you need it: Blizzard says the more advanced Leatherworking recipes need a Tanning Rack.
Rest at your Camp Tent while you level: it tops up rested XP to 5% of a level.
Sit at the camp for at least 1 minute to get its buff. A basic campsite holds 3 camp features, one per player, so agree in the group who places what.

mistakes.mistake: Planning the advanced recipes without a Tanning Rack.
mistakes.fix: Blizzard says they need one. It is the skill-140 camp object, and its blueprint drops from Razorclaw the Butcher in Shadowfang Keep.

steps.text: Train Journeyman at skill 50 and level 10, Expert at skill 125 and level 20, and Artisan at skill 200 and level 35. 300 is the cap.
Build Merchant's Favor by filling Waylaid Crates and handing the sealed crates to Marcy Baker at Three Corners in western Redridge. Craftsman's Writs add reputation.
Spend Favor at the Azeroth Commerce Authority at Three Corners. The Mystic Rugged kit recipe needs Honored and 90 Favor.
Reaching 150, 225 and 300 for the first time in a craft each earns 1 Legacy point. Working Overtime improves your skill-up chance.
Plan your specialization. Forever guides list the same three as Classic 1.12: Dragonscale, Elemental and Tribal Leatherworking.
At 300, earn the certification item that unlocks your profession title. Alliance players get it from the Azeroth Commerce Authority.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting at the Journeyman cap of 150 before training Expert.
mistakes.fix: Expert needs skill 125 and level 20, so train it between 125 and 150.

mistakes.mistake: Following a Classic 1.12 specialization walkthrough as if it were confirmed for Forever.
mistakes.fix: Forever guides list the same three paths, but the quests themselves have not been checked in Forever yet.

201.summary: Gear only you can make, armor kits for the raid, and the market.

steps.text: Make Bind on Pickup pieces such as Wisdom's Leather Boots for yourself.

mistakes.mistake: Promising Wisdom's Leather Boots to a guildmate.
mistakes.fix: They are Bind on Pickup for the leatherworker who makes them.

steps.text: Make Core Armor Kits for tanks: they now give +4 defense instead of +3.
Match the new stat kits to the role: Light for Stamina, Forceful Medium for attack power and Mystic Medium for spell power.
Add the Mystic Rugged kit once you are Honored; the recipe costs 90 Favor.

mistakes.mistake: Selling Core Armor Kits as +3 defense.
mistakes.fix: The Core Armor Kit gives +4 defense in Forever.

steps.text: Armor kits, including the new stat kits, are consumable crafts many roles can use, so test them on the Auction House. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
Check the Auction House before you sell surplus crafts to a vendor: Blizzard's beta notes say many profession-made items sell to vendors for less.

mistakes.mistake: Selling surplus crafts to a vendor out of Classic habit.
mistakes.fix: Many profession-made items sell to vendors for less in Forever, so compare the Auction House first.
